card.title: Exam bank — every board question on plane refraction

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Two questions: Snell's law plus light speed in glass (2023: mu 1.5 gives 2x10^8 m/s) and TIR with its two conditions (2022). Bending tracks speed change (frequency fixed); past the critical angle dense-to-rare, refraction dies and total reflection takes over.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: mu1 sin i = mu2 sin r · mu = c/v · sin C = 1/mu (dense to rare) · slab shift d = t sin(i-r)/cos r

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Snell needs single wavelength (meaning mu varies per colour). TIR needs BOTH denser-to-rarer travel and i beyond C (missing either gives ordinary refraction). Lateral shift needs parallel slab faces.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Glass mu 1.5: v = 2x10^8 m/s, C ~ 41.8 degrees. Diamond mu 2.4: C ~ 24 degrees (sparkle engine). Fibre optics, endoscopes, mirages all run TIR.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): Snell stated (incident/refracted sines ratio constant), v = 3x10^8/1.5 = 2x10^8 m/s. NEB 2022 (2): TIR defined (100 percent reflection past critical) with both conditions named.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Mark-losers: critical angle claimed rare-to-dense; single-mu treatment of white light; polarisation/absorption ignored (Snell tracks direction only).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Wavefront timing across the boundary gives sin i/sin r = c1/c2. Grazing limit r = 90 degrees yields sin C = 1/mu; beyond it no real r satisfies Snell, so reflection takes all.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: TIR conditions: dense-to-rare plus i beyond C (two marks free). mu = c/v converts speeds. C values: glass ~42, water ~49, diamond ~24.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): Snell + glass speed. NEB 2022 (2): TIR + two conditions. That is the complete bank.
